subject: Safety-net rate cap request — temporary accommodation for quantization schedule slip
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>; Beth Carlson <beth@acmehealth.com>
Cc: acme-procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Safety-net rate cap request — temporary accommodation for quantization schedule slip

Hi team / Beth,

Quick summary: Acme is asking us to soften pricing for their pilot because the quantized model we promised in Q2 is slipping into late Q3. They’re concerned their cost run rate during the pilot will be materially higher without the quantized variant. Nikhil flagged this in the deal thread and asked for an exec-level temporary rate cap or similar safety-net.

Asks:
- Exec approval to offer a timeboxed rate cap (not a rebate) for the pilot period (start of pilot -> 90 days) that limits per-token charges to $0.0008 for generation requests.
- Conditions: cap only for pilot environment, data residency unchanged, no public marketing claims.

I’ve attached a one-page proposal and the updated quant timeline. Can Product (Karthik) confirm the expected delivery window and scope? Finance (Laura) — can you quick sanity-check the P&L impact? Marissa — would need your signoff to proceed.

Attachments: rate_safety_net_proposal.xlsx, quant_timeline_v2.pdf

Next step I suggest: internal approval thread today, then a brief email to Beth with terms and an updated mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety-net rate cap request — temporary accommodation for quantization schedule slip

Sofia,

Thanks for the heads-up and the attachments — reviewed the timeline. TL;DR: quantization work hit an unexpected kernel compatibility regression across the multi-gpu hosting stack. Engineering needs ~10 more weeks to complete validation and a limited rollback is risky. That pushes GA for the 4-bit quantized variant to mid-August instead of end-June.

Mitigations we can do now:
- Provide a pre-quantized smaller-footprint variant for constrained workloads (not full parity on throughput).
- Offer KV-cache optimizations and a suggested batching profile so Acme's per-token cost can drop by ~12–15% immediately.

Note: Both mitigations are engineering + runtime config changes, low risk, and should be in place within 1–2 weeks. The full quantized model remains the longer lead item.

Happy to jump on a short call with Acme technical stakeholders to explain tradeoffs.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP Product, Serving Runtime

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Beth Carlson <beth@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety-net rate cap request — temporary accommodation for quantization schedule slip

Internal note then external: Acme is an anchor pilot — if we don’t provide a reasonable accommodation they’ll pause the pilot and push procurement back to Nov, which jeopardizes the full rollout. Beth asked for something simple and fast: "a safety net so we don't overspend during pilot."

Proposed customer-facing language (for Beth):
"Redwood will provide a temporary, timeboxed per-token rate cap for your pilot environment while we finalize the quantized model. This cap is limited to the pilot cluster and applies for up to 90 days from the pilot start date. All other terms remain as-is.

If internal signoff is quick, I’ll send the note to Beth by EOD asking them to confirm the pilot start date and acceptance. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2028-042

Nikhil
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
",

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety-net rate cap request — temporary accommodation for quantization schedule slip

Appreciate the details. I pulled rough modeled P&L against the proposed cap and attached a workbook (rate_safety_net_proposal.xlsx) with scenario rows. Key points:
- If we cap generation at $0.0008/token for 90 days the net ARR impact is roughly a 0.4% hit for 2028 revenue run rate assuming a pilot-to-production conversion.
- Rebate vs rate cap: I prefer a rate cap since it’s simpler operationally (no retro rebates) and reduces auditing burden.
- Controls required: cap must be gated by pilot cluster tag + start/end dates and require a signed email acceptance from Acme.

If Marissa is comfortable with the small top-line impact, I support moving forward with the cap with the gating controls above.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance — Commercial Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety-net rate cap request — temporary accommodation for quantization schedule slip

Approved with conditions:
1) Approve temporary rate cap at $0.0008/token for up to 90 days for Acme pilot only.
2) Legal to insert a short amendment (one paragraph) and require Acme's signed acceptance email. Ops must implement the cluster gating and automated end-date enforcement.
3) No cross-customer precedent: this language must be narrowly scoped to Acme and recorded as an exception with a 1:1 reference to deal ID ACME-2028-042.
4) Product to provide a technical mitigation note (Karthik) to share with Acme so expectations are clear.

Sofia — you have greenlight to communicate terms to Beth once Legal confirms the single-paragraph amendment can be ready in 48 hours. Please copy Laura on the customer acceptance.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Chief Revenue Officer

From: Beth Carlson <beth@acmehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-procurement@acmehealth.com, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 May 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety-net rate cap request — temporary accommodation for quantization schedule slip

Sofia — thank you and please extend our appreciation to the team. We accept the temporary rate cap at $0.0008/token for the pilot and will await the amendment language. Can we confirm the pilot start date as June 1? If Ops gating is needed we’ll coordinate a short window with your team next week.

Best,
Beth
Beth Carlson
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
